paper.title: Representativeness of survey participants in relation to mental disorders: a linkage between national registers and a population-representative survey
paper.journal: International Journal of Population Data Science
paper.code_data_availability: Ethics statement (p. 8-9): 'The study was approved by the Danish Data Protection Agency. …

registers.role: sample frame and linkage; demographics (date of birth, sex)
treatment/exposure and outcome: mental disorder diagnoses before the survey date

registers.years: inpatient contacts since 1977; outpatient or emergency contacts since 1995
registers.role: outcomes: nine general medical conditions (diagnosis criteria in Supplementary Table 3)
variables_mentioned: ICD-10 diagnosis codes listed in Supplementary Table 3

registers.role: outcomes: general medical conditions ascertained from redeemed prescriptions
variables_mentioned: ATC drug codes listed in Supplementary Table 3

registers.years: annual data since 1981; educational level in 2016 used
registers.role: controls: education group (primary/early childhood, secondary, above secondary, missing)

registers.name_in_paper: 2017 Central Denmark Region How are you? survey (Hvordan har du det?)
registers.role: treatment/sample: survey participation and the non-response weights
variables_mentioned: non-response weights (model-based calibration on municipality, sex, age, social background, GP and somatic hospital visits)

linkages: All individuals eligible to participate identified in the Danish Civil Registration System and linked by the unique Central Person Register number to the psychiatric, patient, prescription and education registers
Survey participants linked to the national registers by Statistics Denmark, which anonymised the data; non-responders could not be identified in the registers for ethical reasons

sample.universe: the 1,063,082 individuals in Denmark who met the eligibility criteria for participating in the 2017 Central Denmark Region How are you? survey (16 years of age or older on 10 January 2017 and registered as living in the Central Denmark Region on that date)
selection_rules: aged 16 years or older on 10 January 2017
registered as living within the Central Denmark Region on 10 January 2017, per the Danish Civil Registration System
52,000 persons invited by stratified random selection (stratification ensured coverage of all municipalities; smaller municipalities oversampled)
three analysis populations: the entire eligible population, the survey participants, and the survey participants weighted by Statistics Denmark's non-response weights
general medical conditions ascertained only after individuals reached 1 year of age and from 1995 onwards
sample.period: cross-sectional as of 10 January 2017; mental disorders ascertained 1969 to January 2017, general medical conditions from 1995

construction_notes: Any mental disorder = at least one ICD-10 F code; 10 specific types defined by F-code subgroup with ICD-8 equivalents and a group-specific earliest age of diagnosis (Supplementary Table 2)
Mental disorders ascertained from psychiatric inpatient contacts since 1969 and outpatient or emergency contacts since 1995; ICD-8 before 1994, ICD-10 from 1994

Nine general medical conditions (circulatory, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, urogenital, musculoskeletal, hematological, cancer, neurological) defined as in previous studies from hospital diagnoses and/or redeemed prescriptions, with condition-specific prescription frequency requirements (Supplementary Table 3)

Antihypertensives ascertained only in absence of ischemic heart disease/heart failure, and by diuretics only if no kidney disease; lipid-lowering prescriptions used only if no previous ischemic heart disease
Education group measured in the year prior to the survey (educational level in 2016), with 'missing' kept as a category

Non-response weights supplied by Statistics Denmark, built with a model-based calibration approach on sex, age, municipality of residence, social background and healthcare utilization; they contain no direct information on mental disorders
Frequencies, proportions and chi-squared tests for a type of mental disorder are suppressed ('NS') for a sex if any age group comprised fewer than 5 cases
Survey responses themselves were not used, because they are available only for participants
Analyses run in Stata 16 and Microsoft Excel

key_assumptions.assumption: Register-recorded diagnoses identify who has a mental disorder; the Danish national registers are not a gold standard and hold no information on mental disorders treated only in general practice or by independent psychiatrists and psychologists, or on people who do not seek medical treatment
key_assumptions.supported_by: No test offered; discussed as the first limitation of the study (p. 8)

key_assumptions.assumption: Anyone who had received a mental disorder diagnosis prior to survey eligibility is classified as having a mental disorder; recovery cannot be identified, so misclassification is possible in both directions
key_assumptions.supported_by: No test offered; discussed as the second limitation of the study (p. 8)

key_assumptions.assumption: The study population is conditioned on being eligible to participate in the survey; selection through, for example, excess mortality among people with mental disorders affects survey participants and the eligible population alike
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued in the limitations section; no empirical test (p. 8)
